events.title: The Plague of Athens
events.summary: A mystery epidemic kills up to a quarter of Athens during the Peloponnesian War, described in detail by Thucydides.

events.title: The Antonine Plague
events.summary: Probably smallpox, it spreads through the Roman Empire with soldiers returning from the east.

events.title: The Plague of Justinian
events.summary: The first recorded pandemic of bubonic plague strikes Constantinople and the Mediterranean.

events.title: The Black Death reaches Europe
events.summary: Plague arrives through Black Sea trade routes and goes on to kill a third or more of Europe's population.

events.title: Smallpox devastates Tenochtitlan
events.summary: Smallpox brought by Spanish expeditions kills a huge share of the Aztec capital's population.

events.title: The Great Plague of London
events.summary: The last major plague epidemic in England kills about a quarter of London's people.

events.title: Smallpox inoculation tested in Boston
events.summary: Following knowledge shared by Onesimus, an enslaved West African man, Zabdiel Boylston inoculates Bostonians during an epidemic.

events.title: Edward Jenner tests the first vaccine
events.summary: Jenner inoculates a boy with cowpox and shows it protects against smallpox.

events.title: Semmelweis makes doctors wash their hands
events.summary: Chlorine handwashing cuts deaths from childbed fever on his maternity ward.

events.title: Britain passes its first Public Health Act
events.summary: A General Board of Health is created to improve drains, water and sanitation in towns.

events.title: John Snow traces cholera to the Broad Street pump
events.summary: Mapping deaths around one water pump becomes a founding moment for epidemiology.

events.title: Florence Nightingale reforms the Scutari hospital
events.summary: Her sanitation reforms and statistics during the Crimean War transform nursing and hospital care.

events.title: Robert Koch identifies the tuberculosis bacterium
events.summary: His discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis proves TB is infectious.

events.title: Pasteur's rabies vaccine saves a boy
events.summary: Louis Pasteur treats nine-year-old Joseph Meister after a rabid dog bite, and the boy survives.

events.title: Ronald Ross shows mosquitoes carry malaria
events.summary: Working in Secunderabad, Ross finds the malaria parasite in an Anopheles mosquito.

events.title: Yellow fever linked to mosquitoes
events.summary: Walter Reed's commission, building on Carlos Finlay's work, proves mosquitoes spread yellow fever.

events.title: Typhoid Mary is identified
events.summary: Cook Mary Mallon becomes the first known healthy carrier of typhoid in the US.

events.title: The Manchurian plague and the first modern face masks
events.summary: Wu Lien-teh leads the response to pneumonic plague and champions gauze masks.

events.title: The 1918 influenza pandemic
events.summary: One of the first recorded outbreaks is at an army camp in Kansas. The pandemic kills an estimated 50 million people worldwide.

events.title: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
events.summary: A mouldy petri dish at St Mary's Hospital leads to the first antibiotic.

events.title: The World Health Organization is founded
events.summary: Its constitution defines health as complete physical, mental and social well-being.

events.title: The Great Smog of London
events.summary: Four days of coal smoke kill thousands and lead to the Clean Air Act of 1956.

events.title: Salk's polio vaccine is declared safe and effective
events.summary: The field trial results are announced to a packed room and church bells ring across the US.

events.title: Minamata disease is identified
events.summary: Mercury poisoning from factory waste in the bay causes severe neurological disease.

events.title: Marburg virus is discovered
events.summary: Lab workers handling monkeys from Uganda fall ill in Marburg and Frankfurt.

events.title: First recognised Ebola outbreak
events.summary: A mission hospital near the Ebola River sees a deadly new haemorrhagic fever.

events.title: The last natural case of smallpox
events.summary: Hospital cook Ali Maow Maalin recovers. Smallpox is declared eradicated in 1980.

events.title: The Alma-Ata Declaration on primary health care
events.summary: Countries commit to health for all through primary care.

events.title: First reports of what becomes AIDS
events.summary: The CDC describes unusual pneumonia in five young men in Los Angeles.

events.title: Bhopal gas disaster
events.summary: A methyl isocyanate leak from a pesticide plant exposes over half a million people.

events.title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
events.summary: A reactor explosion spreads radioactive fallout across Europe.

events.title: SARS spreads from a Hong Kong hotel
events.summary: A new coronavirus reaches about 30 countries before it is contained.

events.title: Cholera follows Haiti's earthquake
events.summary: Cholera reaches Haiti for the first time in a century, infecting over 800,000 people.

events.title: West Africa Ebola epidemic
events.summary: The largest Ebola epidemic to date, with over 28,000 cases across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

events.title: The Flint water crisis
events.summary: A switch in water source leaves residents exposed to lead.

events.title: Zika and microcephaly in Brazil
events.summary: Doctors in northeast Brazil link a surge in babies born with microcephaly to Zika virus.

events.title: COVID-19 emerges
events.summary: A novel coronavirus is identified and becomes a pandemic within months.

events.title: Africa is certified free of wild polio
events.summary: Nigeria's last wild case was in 2016, and the whole region is certified four years later.

events.title: WHO recommends the first malaria vaccine
events.summary: RTS,S is recommended for children after pilots in Malawi, Ghana and Kenya.
